item.title: Legal & Data Protection Officer
item.description: Legal & Data Protection Officer Eurofound - The European Foundation for the Improvement of Living & Working Conditions Dublin, Ireland JOB CONTEXT & DUTIES The Organisational Support Unit provides a range of services for the efficient development and implementation of Eurofound’s operations through various planning and management information systems, workflows and management and performance reporting tools. The Unit is also responsible for supporting the Executive Director and staff in areas of legal advice, data protection, document management and internal control. The duties will require to work on a variety of organisation-wide tasks in good collaboration with colleagues in the Unit as well as with colleagues across the organisation. The Legal & Data Protection Officer will be based in the Organisational Support Unit and will contribute to the achievement of Eurofound’s objectives by providing legal advice and support on the interpretation and application of the legal framework governing Eurofound’s operational and administrative activities. The successful candidate will also be appointed as the Data Protection Officer overseeing Eurofound’s data protection strategy and implementation in accordance with the applicable Regulation (EU) 2018/1725. The duties of the post include: Legal advice and consultation: Providing input in respect of all legal aspects relevant to the functioning of Eurofound, including on matters related to staff and financial regulations, governance structure, data protection, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and contractual matters including intellectual property rights. Drafting legal opinions and documents on the application and interpretation of Eurofound’s legal framework as well as any other applicable legal provisions of Union law. Drafting decisions of the Management Board or other bodies of Eurofound’s governance structure. Contributing to the preparation and implementation of arrangements with other Union institutions and bodies, and other external partners. Cooperating with external legal advisors; including those that may represent the Agency in litigation before the Court of Justice of the European Union. Data Protection: Informing and advising staff on their obligations pursuant to the Data Protection Regulation. Preparing and monitoring policies and guidelines on data protection. Conducting regular assessments. Maintaining records of all data processing activities Serving as the point of contact between the Agency and the European Data Protection Supervisor (EDPS). General: Collaborating with staff in achieving compliance with the legal framework and awareness of data protection requirements in the agency’s operations. Providing training and coaching in regulatory compliance – in collaboration with staff in HR, Internal control and ICT (on AI and cybersecurity). Representing Eurofound in inter-agency networks on legal matters and data protection. Other tasks assigned by the Head of Unit. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE REQUIRED The selection procedure is open to candidates who, by the closing date for applications, fulfil the following conditions: ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA Citizenship of one of the Member States of the European Union, entitled to full rights as a citizen; Have fulfilled any obligations imposed by the laws concerning military service; Have a thorough knowledge of one official language of the European Union and a satisfactory knowledge (level B2) of another language of the Union. As English is the daily working language of Eurofound, a high level of proficiency in English (C1) is required to a level necessary for the performance of the duties. at least a level of education which corresponds to completed university studies of at least three years attested by a diploma. SELECTION CRITERIA Candidates will be shortlisted on the basis of the following criteria: • University degree in law and/or advanced studies in law with a focus on some or all of: Administrative law, EU law and data protection; • At least three years’ experience in areas of relevance to this role in legal practice or advice and data protection; • Experience of administrative and routine work and evidence of a clear understanding of the duties that the role of Legal and Data Protection Officer entails, preferably within the framework of EU institutions and bodies. In addition to the above, candidates who are invited for testing and interview will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria: Excellent writing skills; Excellent verbal communication skills with the ability to explain the practical implications of rules and regulations through different formats supporting organisational learning and compliance; Excellent digital skills; Excellent analytical skills; Ability to manage own workload and adapt as necessary to changing demands and hard deadlines. Collaborative team player, capable of working autonomously when necessary; Ability to work effectively in an international or multicultural environment; Proof of meeting eligibility criteria - by means of appropriate documents (copies of educational certificates, references from employers, etc.) - must be provided if requested. Apply Now Don't forget to mention EuroBrussels when applying.

item.description: Legal Coordinator CoB - Council of Bureaux Brussels, Belgium CONTRACT: Full-time, open-ended START: Ideally autumn 2026 About COB COB manages the International Motor Insurance 'Green Card' system and coordinates the daily operation of the European Motor Insurance Directives. Operating under the aegis of the United Nations, COB works closely with EU Institutions to support the free movement of vehicles, and the settlement of international motor accident claims across Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. Role purpose COB is looking for a Legal Coordinator to join its Secretariat in Brussels. The Legal Coordinator provides legal, technical and organisational support to COB committees and working groups, and acts as a trusted point of contact for members and external stakeholders. Key responsibilities Committee & working group support: prepare agendas and supporting papers; attend meetings and draft clear minutes; coordinate follow-up and circulate outcomes. Legal and technical work: prepare legal and technical analysis; produce questionnaires and information material; contribute to policy and operational documentation; monitor jurisprudence of the Court of Justice of the European Union. Member and stakeholder liaison: liaise with Member Bureaux, Guarantee Funds, Compensation Bodies and Information Centres; maintain constructive contact with external partners (including United Nations Economic Commission for Europe and the European Commission). International coordination: support exchanges with the insurance sector and European Institutions; travel mainly in Europe from time to time when required. Candidate at a glance Legal profile: Law degree or equivalent legal background Languages: Excellent written and oral English; other EU languages an asset Working style: Organised, collaborative, independent and comfortable in a small team Legal Coordinator - detailed profile A practical, member-facing legal role in an international organisation with a clear public-interest mission. Candidate profile: Degree in Law; a strong equivalent legal qualification may also be considered if the overall profile is relevant; Experience in motor insurance, claims handling or insurance more generally is an asset; Excellent written and oral communication skills in English; Knowledge of other EU languages is an asset; Right to work in Belgium/the EU or a valid work permit; Good organisational skills, sound judgement and attention to detail; Strong interpersonal skills: able to work independently and as part of a small international team; Good computer literacy and ability to work with standard office tools. The offer Full-time open-ended contract; Pleasant and international working environment at COB Secretariat; Competitive salary package with extra-legal benefits, including group insurance, hospitalisation insurance, mobility budget, luncheon vouchers and 13 th month; Flexible organisation of work (including telework) where the agenda allows; Training and education opportunities in line with the position; Office on Avenue Louise, easily accessible by public transport. Application procedure How to apply: Please send a CV and cover letter in English explaining how your skills and experience match the role. Send to: Alexandra Sibille, Administrative Manager & HR Coordinator, at hr@cobx.org . Deadline: 30 September 2026 Only selected candidates will be contacted for further steps of the recruitment and selection procedure. COB is committed to conducting the recruitment and selection procedure in a professional, respectful and confidential manner. Don't forget to mention EuroBrussels when applying.

item.description: Policy Assistant for European Institutions (CIP Internship) (Six Months) EEB - European Environmental Bureau Brussels, Belgium € 1 300 per month net Come join Europe’s largest network of environmental citizens’ organisations and contribute as a policy assistant with a Convention d’Immersion Professionelle (CIP) to its work on the next EU budget (multi annual financial framework - MFF) for a better future where people and nature thrive together. About us The EEB is the largest network of environmental citizens’ organisations in Europe. We bring together over 190 member organisations from more than 40 countries, representing some 30 million individual members and supporters. We advocate for progressive policies to create a better future where people and nature thrive together. About the internship The EEB offers paid internships under a Convention d’Immersion Professionelle (CIP), which is a scheme for organisations based in the Brussels Region under the supervision of Bruxelles Formation. A CIP internship is therefore a paid internship with a trilateral contract between the intern, the EEB and Bruxelles Formation and is regulated under Belgian law. A CIP contract does not constitute an employment relationship, and an intern is therefore not an employee of the organisation. CIP internships are only available to graduates, that is, individuals who are not students anymore. CIP contracts cannot be offered to enrolled students. Interns who are neither Belgian citizens nor graduates from Belgian universities are, according to the legal framework, eligible for CIP contracts for up to 12 months (as opposed to 6 months for Belgians and Belgian graduates). Our commitment to fairness, equality, diversity and wellbeing The EEB strives to be a fair, inclusive, safe place and a welcoming and learning organisation. We are an equal opportunity employer and encourage applications from a diverse range of candidates. Your experience matters. Please consult our Diversity, Equality and Inclusion Policy . Please do not use pictures in your CV. Do leave out any information that may contribute to unconscious bias such as reference to your nationality, date or place of birth. We respect our employees’ lives outside of work, support colleagues in care roles, and take work-life balance and wellbeing seriously. How You Will Have an Impact As our policy assistant for European Institutions, you will join a strategic horizontal and cross cutting team of the organisation managed directly by the EEB Policy Director and supported by the European Institutions policy officer that covers essential horizontal policies. You will in particular be given the chance to contribute to and influence a set of key legislations that are instrumental to the future of EU environmental and climate actions while monitoring other key horizontal developments impacting EU environmental laws such as simplification and key milestones (EU presidencies etc.). Your role will also provide you with the opportunity to closely engage with EEB national members and other partners such as other EU large environmental networks. What You Will Actually Do Support the coordination efforts of EEB MFF advocacy (in particular help with the monitoring of relevant legislative developments, meetings with EEB members or colleagues, ensure good internal communication flows on the topic); Support mobilisation and advocacy efforts of the broader environmental coalition working on MFF (take part in the weekly meetings of the coalition and help prepare them, support collective actions when needed (calls with members, gatherings, advocacy meetings)); Support the EEB European Institutions and Governance team horizontal policy work (in particular help with the weekly newsletter, help with the different horizontal policy task forces (minutes, follow up)). Who You Are As EEB’s future policy assistant for European Institutions (CIP internship) , you will have a Bachelor/master's degree OR relevant experience, a basic understanding of European legislation related to the Multi Annual Financial Framework and a strong interest in working for an environmental organisation. item.description: Vertaler en Conferentietolk (m/v) Moedertaal Nederlands Eureca Strasbourg, France KLAAR VOOR EEN NIEUWE UITDAGING? De Centrale Commissie voor de Rijnvaart (CCR) heeft sinds 1815 als belangrijkste taak het waarborgen van de veiligheid en de welvaart van de Rijnvaart . Deze internationale organisatie staat bekend om haar belangrijke rol in de binnenvaart en is actief op het snijvlak van technische, sociale en milieuvraagstukken. Het wervingsbureau Eureca zoekt voor deze organisatie een vertaler en conferentietolk (m/v) met Nederlands als moedertaal , ter versterking van het team van vertalers. Functie op basis van een tijdelijk contract (duur: 4 jaar) met zicht op omzetting naar een vast contract. Mooi kantoor in het hart van Straatsburg met de mogelijkheid tot gedeeltelijk thuiswerken . Jouw taken omvatten: Het vertalen van redactionele, technische en soms politiek gevoelige teksten vanuit het Duits en het Frans naar het Nederlands , met inachtneming van deadlines, kwaliteitseisen en de geldende terminologie, waarbij je je werklast zelfstandig en flexibel indeelt; Het volgen van ontwikkelingen binnen de werkterreinen van de organisatie en van terminologische en taalkundige ontwikkelingen, en het actualiseren van vertaalgeheugens en woordenlijsten; Nauwe samenwerking met de auteurs over taalkundige en stilistische keuzes; Simultaan vertalen van het Duits naar het Nederlands en omgekeerd tijdens vergaderingen, werkgroepen en gesprekken met tolk die plaatsvinden op het hoofdkantoor van de organisatie; Voorbereiding van elke tolkopdracht: bestudering van de werkdocumenten, de agenda en videomateriaal, gericht terminologisch onderzoek. WAT DEZE FUNCTIE AANTREKKELIJK MAAKT Het opbouwen van specialistische expertise op technisch, politiek en sectoraal gebied; Goede begeleiding tijdens je inwerkperiode; Werken in een internationale, dynamische en stimulerende werkomgeving. JE BENT GESCHIKT VOOR DEZE FUNCTIE ALS Je bent afgestudeerd met een master in vertalen en conferentietolken en beheerst naast je moedertaal, het Nederlands, ook het Duits uitstekend. Een goede beheersing van het Frans (B2 – C1) is een pluspunt voor vertalingen naar het Nederlands; Je hebt minimaal 3 jaar ervaring in vertalen en tolken; Je bent georganiseerd, nauwgezet en werkt graag in teamverband. Solliciteer door je cv en motivatiebrief te sturen naar: cbouquet@eureca-rh.com . Traducteur H/F Natif Néerlandais Eureca Strasbourg, France PRÊT(E) POUR UN NOUVEAU DÉFI ? La Commission centrale pour la navigation du Rhin (CCNR) est une organisation internationale de plus de 200 ans dont le siège est à Strasbourg. Elle compte cinq États membres (Allemagne, Belgique, France, Pays-Bas et Suisse) et a pour mission principale d’assurer la sécurité et la prospérité de la navigation rhénane. La CCNR est une organisation à la pointe de l’innovation pour permettre à la flotte rhénane d’être à l’avant-garde et de faire face aux défis d’aujourd’hui: la digitalisation, le verdissement, l’automatisation, l’adaptation au changement climatique, les qualifications du personnel ou encore la position économique du secteur. Au-delà du Rhin, de nombreuses activités de la CCNR sont maintenant réalisées dans un cadre européen. Le cabinet de recrutement Eureca recherche pour cette organisation un Traducteur H/F, de langue maternelle néerlandaise , pour renforcer son équipe linguistique. Poste en CDD (durée de 4 ans) et perspective de transformation en CDI. De beaux locaux en plein cœur de Strasbourg avec possibilité de télétravail partiel . LA MISSION QUE L’ON VOUS PROPOSE Rattaché(e) à la secrétaire générale et au sein de l’équipe de traducteurs, vos missions incluent: (80% du temps) Traduction de l’allemand et du français vers le néerlandais de textes rédactionnels, techniques et parfois politiquement sensibles, dans le respect des délais, des exigences de qualité et de la terminologie en vigueur en organisant votre charge de travail avec autonomie et flexibilité; Veille sur les domaines d'activité de l’organisation ainsi que sur les nouveautés terminologiques et linguistiques et mise à jour des mémoires de traduction et glossaires; Collaboration étroite avec les auteurs sur les choix linguistiques et stylistiques; (20% du temps) Ponctuellement, interprétation simultanée de l’allemand vers le néerlandais et inversement à l’occasion de réunions, groupes de travail et entretiens interprétés se tenant au siège de l’organisation; Préparation de chaque mission d’interprétation: prise de connaissance des documents de travail, de l’ordre du jour, des support vidéo, recherche terminologique ciblée. VOUS AIMEREZ Développer une véritable expertise sectorielle, technique ou politique, au fil des textes; Bénéficier d'un accompagnement lors de votre intégration pour faciliter votre prise de poste; Evoluer dans un environnement de travail international, dynamique et stimulant. VOUS RÉUSSIREZ À CE POSTE SI Diplômé(e) d’un Master en traduction , vous avez une excellente maîtrise de l’allemand en plus de votre langue maternelle, le néerlandais. Une bonne maîtrise du français (B2 – C1) est un atout; Idéalement, vous êtes diplômé(e) d’un Master en interprétation avec l’allemand et le néerlandais comme langues de travail ; Vous bénéficiez d’une expérience de 3 ans minimum en traduction et idéalement en interprétation; Organisé(e), vous êtes rigoureux(se) et vous appréciez le travail en équipe. item.description: Civil Society Fund Transnational Officer Position - VA 29/2026 FMO - Financial Mechanism Office Brussels, Belgium From € 117,072 per year Are you a dynamic and highly motivated professional looking to make a positive impact in Europe? Join our team in the Civil Society Fund at the Financial Mechanism Office (FMO) in Brussels to work on strengthening a vibrant and resilient civil society protecting democracy, the rule of law and human rights. You will be responsible for the new component called “Civil Society Fund -Transnational (CSF-TN)” working at European level. The position is open to nationals of the EEA EFTA States (Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway) and to the nationals of the Beneficiary States of EEA and Norway Grants (Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia). About us: The Financial Mechanism Office (FMO) - affiliated with the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) - is the international secretariat carrying out the day-to-day management of the EEA and Norway Grants. The Grants are Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway’s contribution to reducing economic and social disparities in the European Economic Area (EEA) and strengthen bilateral relations and partnerships between the Donor States and the 15 Beneficiary States (Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia). The EEA Grants are financed by the three donor countries whereas Norway Grants are financed solely by Norway. The current funding period has a total budget of 3.2 billion euros. The programmes in this funding period will focus on these overall priorities: European green transition; Democracy, rule of law and human rights; Social inclusion and resilience. Why join the FMO? We offer more than just a job. We offer a stimulating and diverse international workplace with a trust-based culture. Our team of more than 60 employees from the EEA region brings a rich blend of experiences and knowledge to our daily operations. We are committed to fostering a collaborative and respectful environment where you can advance your career. Every day, our work is driven by a shared goal: a green, democratic and resilient Europe where everyone can take a meaningful part in shaping their lives. We work closely with the Ministries of Foreign Affairs of the Donor States (Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway), the 15 Beneficiary States and various international partners. Learn more: If you are ready to take on a rewarding challenge and be part of a dedicated team working towards improving economic and social equality and strengthening cooperation and partnerships in Europe, we encourage you to apply. For more details about our work and the opportunities we offer, please visit our website at www.eeagrants.org . Scope: You will be part of the Civil Society Team within the Funds and Horizontal Concerns Unit, reporting to the Unit’s Head. The Civil Society Fund Transnational (CSF-TN) is a newly established instrument which aims at strengthening capacity, cooperation, and resilience of institutions and civil society to protect and promote democracy, the rule of law, and human rights at European level. The Financial Mechanism Office (FMO) acts as the Fund Operator on behalf of the Donors. The thematic focus of the CSF-TN is civic space and civil society engagement; information integrity and disinformation; and competence and knowledge development for democratic resilience. The CSF-TN Officer is responsible for the overall day-to-day management of the fund. The position combines operational fund management responsibilities with coordination of policy and programme content expertise to ensure that CSF-TN initiatives are aligned with the objectives of the EEA and Norway Grants. The position will involve external representation and engagement with relevant stakeholders; travel will be required. You may be required to work in other areas, according to the needs and priorities of the FMO. Main Responsibilities and tasks: Administration and compliance: As Fund Operator, the FMO is responsible for the technical, administrative and financial management of the CSF-TN. The CSF-TN Officer will: Manage the full grant lifecycle. Follow up grant agreements, work plans and reporting requirements, organise annual meetings and monitor implementation progress, risks, budgets and results across the portfolio; Coordinate closely with legal, finance and management colleagues to ensure sound financial management, and compliance with applicable regulations, Donor requirements and principles of accountability and transparency. Coordination of the CSF-TN portfolio: Responsibilities include: Oversee the CSF-TN portfolio, ensuring its effective implementation and alignment with EEA and Norway Grants objectives, following Donor priorities and Senior Management guidance; Facilitate synergies between the CSF-TN, initiatives implemented by the International Partners Organisations, Civil Society Funds and other relevant EEA and Norway Grants initiatives; Analyse trends, risks and opportunities on the thematic focus of the CSF-TN; Assess the relevance and added value of proposed initiatives in cooperation with relevant FMO colleagues; Support Donor engagement through briefing notes and strategic analysis; Represent the FMO in meetings with European networks, civil society organisations, think tanks, foundations and international partners. Qualifications: A Master’s degree in a relevant field. Required Experience: At least 6 years of relevant professional experience; Experience in grant management, programme or project management; Experience working with civil society organisations, international organisations, public bodies or European networks; Experience in managing complex stakeholder relationships. Desired experience: Knowledge of European civil society ecosystems and networks; Experience working on democratic governance, civic space or information integrity. Required skills: Strong project and portfolio management skills; Knowledge of grant management, compliance and financial oversight; Strong organisational skills; Strong analytical skills and drafting skills; Ability to work autonomously and proactively; Strong interpersonal skills; Presentation skills; ability to present complex matters clearly. A great work environment and strong teamwork define the FMO, and we look for candidates who actively contribute to both. Language: Excellent oral and written communication skills in English (the working language of the FMO). Fluency in any of the Donor or Beneficiary State languages would be an advantage. Employment terms: Job reference: VA 29/2026 Duration of appointment: This is a fixed-term contract for three years. The contract is renewable once, subject to the renewal being in the interest of the FMO and to a decision on the new funding period following the current Financial Mechanisms. Start date: As soon as possible Grade: A4 A nnual starting salary: EUR 117,072 Appointments are normally made at step 1 of the grade. The Managing Director of the FMO reserves the right to appoint a candidate at a level different from that advertised. The FMO is an employer dedicated to the principles of diversity and equality. We are committed to promoting and nurturing a diverse and inclusive workplace, with a healthy work-life balance. FMO offers a hybrid working model for its staff. Subject to the requirements of the role, operational needs, and in agreement with their line manager, staff may work up to 40% of their weekly working hours from a location other than the office according to the current policy. The duty station for all FMO staff is Brussels, Belgium. We offer stimulating and meaningful work in a diverse international environment, with the opportunity to collaborate with highly skilled professionals from across Europe. Salaries and related payments are exempt from taxation in the EFTA Member States, and as regulated in headquarters agreements, in the EFTA host states. Depending on the candidate’s family status, and individual circumstances, additional benefits and allowances may apply. Candidates should carefully consider their individual tax circumstances. This is particularly important where personal circumstances may give rise to tax obligations in countries other than the EFTA Member States of the EFTA host states. For questions related to the recruitment process, please contact us by email: fmorecruitment@efta.int . In case of technical issues with the recruitment tool, please contact: hr.support@efta.int . Please note that only applications received via FMO’s recruitment tool will be considered. Deadline for submission of applications: Wednesday, 28 October 2026 (midnight, Brussels time) . item.description: Communications Trainee ChargeUp Europe Brussels, Belgium About ChargeUp Europe ChargeUp Europe is the voice of the electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure industry. Our growing membership stands for an EV charging infrastructure roll-out that starts from the consumer needs, makes EV driving convenient across borders, and promotes an open-market model supported by open standards and protocols. The trainee will assist the ChargeUp Europe team in all communications activities and projects, including (but not limited to) helping with planning and executing events, supporting the delivery of our communications workplan, and developing content for our social media channels, while servicing members’ needs. This position will offer an opportunity to develop a broad range of communications skills, both through direct experience and by exposure to a network of seasoned communications professionals from the membership. Expected tasks 1. Social media & communications outreach: Creating engaging social media content – both short and long-form – primarily for LinkedIn, ensuring alignment with ChargeUp Europe’s visual identity; Designing clear, meaningful data visualisations and infographics to distil complex information into accessible content; Proactive outreach to stakeholders (e.g. podcast guests and hosts) and support in coordinating activities related to campaigns, podcasts and thematic series; Assisting in drafting written content for social media channels and the ChargeUp Europe website, as well as internal communication tasks and content-creation. 2. Ad-hoc assistance to the Communications Coordinator: Providing administrative and communication support, including document formatting, research, and external communications where needed; Offering ad-hoc assistance in communicating with members and handling day-to-day matters; Collecting, synthesising and analysing information from diverse sources, including data gathering, stakeholder mapping and rapid review of reports to extract key insights. 3. Creative thinking & content development: Contributing fresh, creative ideas to support communications, events and stakeholder engagement; Helping to develop concepts, visuals and messaging for campaigns, events and other formats; Keeping the ChargeUp Europe website up to date; Draft the ChargeUp Europe quarterly newsletter. 4. Logistical support for events: Providing logistical support for online and onsite events (webinars, workshops, presentations), including links, invitations and communication kits. 5. Service to the members: Responding to communications-related requests from ChargeUp Europe members and supporting member-facing activities. Please note that this list is non-exhaustive, and other tasks may be performed under this role. Required skills and competencies Master’s degree in communications or other relevant field; A basic understanding of the European policy landscape and EU institutions; Excellent writing skills in English; Interest in e-mobility; Good interpersonal and organisational skills; Experience in writing for social media, particularly LinkedIn; Experience with Canva. Our offer Targeted start date: asap. Duration: until July 2027. Contract type: CIP (la convention d’immersion professionnelle), full time, based in Brussels (flexible hybrid working regime) Renumeration: per CIP requirements Hiring process Interested candidates should send their application in English by 2 November 2026 COB at the latest to secretariat@chargeupeurope.eu , mentioning “Communications trainee” in the subject line. Please note that interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis: applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible, as the search will be stopped once a suitable candidate has been identified. The application should include: a CV; a cover letter, not written by AI. The cover should not be a repetition of your resume, but a document of maximum 2 pages covering the 4 questions below: What is your motivation for joining ChargeUp Europe; Tell us about a piece of content you made (post, video, newsletter, flyer…) that didn't land the way you hoped. What do you think went wrong, and what would you change? (Include a link or screenshot.); Find an organization similar to ours that does communications better. Show us one example and explain why it works; Pick one of our Linkedln posts from the 4 weeks. What would you keep, and what would you have done differently? a selection of 3 writing examples, preferably across channels/formats; a canva visual you developed. Please note that ChargeUp Europe will not consider applications that are not complete. ChargeUp Europe values diversity and encourages applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion or ethnic background. Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for interviews. Please note that applicants must be authorised to work in the EU.
